sources.title: Lie Symmetry Analysis of the One-Dimensional Saint-Venant-Exner Model
sources.relevance: direct E symmetry and reduction source
sources.equation_closure_domain: h_t+(hu)_x=0; (hu)_t+(hu^2+g h^2/2)_x+g h B_x=0; B_t+xi Q_x=0; Q=A_g u^m; m>=1, source cites empirical 1<=m<=4. For noninteger m, real smooth use requires a sign chart such as u>0 because the paper prints u^m rather than |u|^(m-1)u.
reductions: X3=t*d_t+x*d_x: chi=x/t; one first-order rational ODE for u(chi), with h=(u-chi)^2/(2g) and B by quadrature (Eqs.40-42).
X1+alpha*X4 and X2+alpha*X4: elementary closed-form spatial/time families (Eqs.45-48).
X3+alpha*X4: coupled rational first-order ODE system for u,h,b (Eqs.49-53), no general solution supplied.
X1+alpha*X2+beta*X4: after d sigma=Kbar d Sigma, linear first-order system and exponential u,h,b (Eqs.58-62); sigma(Sigma) remains implicit.
Cubic m=3 X5: three first-order ODEs, then a claimed Abel equation and one power branch (Eqs.63-71).
Cubic mixed X2+alpha*X5 and X3+alpha*X5: coupled first-order systems; alpha=-1 yields two explicit power-law families (Eqs.72-79).
discrepancies: Printed Eq.(25) gives X5=t*d_t-2u*d_u-h*d_h-2B*d_B, but the Section 4.10 ansatz and the project's direct check require t*d_t-u*d_u-2h*d_h-2B*d_B.
The source does not solve an initial-boundary value problem; its final discussion gives only invariance conditions for admissible data.
Its power closure is not the thresholded or signed Grass law on a zero-velocity/interface branch.

sources.title: Lie Symmetries and Similarity Solutions for a Shallow-Water Model with Bed Elevation in Lagrange Variables
sources.relevance: direct P symmetry and reduction source; cites S01 and S05
sources.equation_closure_domain: Starts from the same E power closure Q=A_g u^m, then sets phi_t=u and phi_s=1/h. Its printed bed equation is B_t+beta phi_t^(m-1) phi_ts/phi_s=0 and yields the printed third-order scalar Eq.(7). The local chart requires phi_s>0 and a real branch for phi_t^(m-1).
reductions: X4 common scaling phi=t Phi(s/t): printed third-order ODE Eq.(24) and a cubic singular power profile.
Cubic X5 with sigma=s t^2, phi=phi(sigma): third-order Eq.(25), derivative reduction Eq.(26), then claimed first-order Abel-type Eq.(27) and a power profile.
Traveling X1+alpha X2: third-order Eq.(28), derivative reduction Eq.(29), claimed maximal eight-symmetry linearization, autonomous first-order Eq.(30), and claimed closed form Eq.(31).
X1+alpha X3 and X2+alpha X3: identity/quadratic families (Eqs.32 and surrounding text).
Shifted traveling X1+alpha X2+alpha3 X3: third-order Eq.(33), then claimed implicit quadrature Eq.(34).

solutions.exact_closed_form: singular power and simple polynomial families

discrepancies: Under the declared pullback of an Eulerian bed field, material differentiation adds -(phi_t/phi_s)B_s. Thus P is not the project-derived corrected scalar M.
The existing exact audit refutes the displayed Eqs.(24)-(31), (33) and literal (34) as universal formulas; it separately verifies the generators and singular power profile.
The audit finds an omitted m=1 symmetry stratum X6=t*d_phi, missing optimal-system orbit families, and two sign errors in Table 1.
The source calls the cubic profile decaying although phi=a s^(1/3)t^(2/3) grows at fixed s>0; singularity at t=0 alone is not a shock certificate.
The conclusion first says the IVP was examined and then says it was not discussed; no source numerical initial data are supplied.

sources.title: An analytical solution of the shallow water system coupled to the Exner equation
sources.relevance: direct E exact benchmark, not a Lie classification
sources.equation_closure_domain: Eqs.(1)-(3) with q_b=kappa(tau_b^*-tau_cr^*)^p sqrt((s-1)g d_s^3), rewritten q_b=A u_e^(2p); assumes smooth flow, constant discharge q=hu, tau_b^*>tau_cr^*, and stationary h,u.
reductions: The ansatz forces q_b=alpha x+beta and z_b=-alpha t+z_b0(x); the momentum balance integrates algebraically to z_b0=-(u^3+2gq)/(2gu)+C.

solutions.numerical: relaxation-scheme validation of the exact profile

discrepancies: This is an exact restricted benchmark, not a solution of arbitrary data and not evidence for a maximal symmetry algebra.
Its threshold active branch excludes the inactive/interface problem.

sources.title: On the influence of the thickness of the sediment moving layer in the definition of the bedload transport formula in Exner systems
sources.relevance: direct closure/domain warning and analytical extended-SVE family
sources.model: extended E with moving layer z_m and static erodible layer z_f
sources.equation_closure_domain: Four-field erosion-deposition system Eq.(2), or total-bed E Eq.(3), with q_b tilde=z_m v_b. Eq.(17) uses stress threshold, z_m, erosion/deposition constants and porosity; it reduces to a classical flux only in quasi-uniform regime.
reductions: Appendix B assumes q=hu constant, h=h(x), Darcy-Weisbach stress, m1=0, tau_cr^*=0, and constant affine-flux coefficients A,B. It obtains an algebraic implicit equation for z_m(x), then u,h,z_b, and z_f(t,x)=-At+z_b(0,x)-z_m(x).
discrepancies: The extra z_m,z_f dynamics and threshold law are not interchangeable with Q=A_g u^m in S01/S02.
The paper itself reports missing experimental inputs such as z_m and closure parameters for one bore comparison.

sources.title: Shallow water equations in Lagrangian coordinates: Symmetries, conservation laws and its preservation in difference models
sources.venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation 89, 105343
sources.model: one-dimensional shallow-water equations with prescribed bottom h(x); no Exner evolution
sources.equation_closure_domain: Eulerian SWE Eqs.(1)-(2), mass coordinate ds=rho dx-rho u dt, and potential equation x_tt-x_ss/x_s^3-h_x=0. The linear-bottom case maps to flat bottom; x_s!=0 is required.
reductions: After the paper rescales the flat-bottom pressure normalization so that Eq.(29) becomes Eq.(35), traveling x=psi(s-alpha t) gives psi''(alpha^2 psi'^3-2)=0, hence affine or constant-slope branches.
For that rescaled equation, dilation x=s^(1/3)psi(t) gives psi^2 psi''+12=0 and the particular exact x=(54 s t^2)^(1/3).
The paper also derives invariant difference reductions and a discrete first integral, which are not automatically continuous SVE integrals.

solutions.implicit_quadrature: discrete Cauchy relation in the scheme

discrepancies: No evolving bed or sediment-flux closure is present, so its variational/Noether structure cannot be transferred to P, M or E without a fresh derivation.

sources.title: Double reduction of PDEs from the association of symmetries with conservation laws with applications
sources.model: general scalar PDE or PDE system with two independent variables
sources.equation_closure_domain: Requires a verified symmetry associated with a verified conserved vector; Theorem 3.1 is stated for a qth-order scalar PDE in two independent variables.
reductions: The associated conservation law in canonical coordinates integrates to T^r=k, lowering the invariant ODE from order q to q-1; examples include heat, sine-Gordon, BBM and one-dimensional gas dynamics.
discrepancies: Association is an extra condition; a symmetry alone does not supply the first integral.
The paper does not prove that any SVE current is associated with the proposed E/P/M generators.

unsolved_leads: Re-derive and register every E optimal-system reduction with the corrected cubic generator before solving any ODE.
For P and M separately, start from an undivided pullback, search exact currents/first integrals, and keep singular leading-coefficient branches outside divided normal form.
Test Sjoberg association explicitly for each candidate E/P/M generator-current pair; do not infer double reduction from symmetry alone.
Use S03 and S04 restricted analytical families as independent E regression targets, not as arbitrary-data solutions.
Repeat closure-specific analysis for signed Grass, threshold active/inactive/interface branches, and the moving-layer state extension.
No retained primary source classifies or solves M; maximality, global continuation, shock admissibility, and compatible initial-boundary data remain open.
